function: Channel prediction: forecasts future MIMO-OFDM CSI for L = 4 steps from P = 16 historical steps, in high-mobility TDD and FDD systems (pp. 4, 9).
system: Massive MIMO-OFDM downlink; BS 4x4 dual-polarized UPA (32 ports), UE with an omni-directional antenna, 2.4 GHz, 48 subcarriers, 8.64 MHz; no RIS (p. 9).
method: Mamba-2 selective state-space model with dual-domain CSI/CIR input, parameter-shared temporal Mamba blocks, bidirectional Mamba and lightweight attention; supervised NMSE loss, AdamW, 500 epochs (pp. 5-9).
data_channel: QuaDRiGa, 3GPP-compliant UMa-NLoS (training) and UMi-NLoS, UMi-LoS (transfer testing); 10,000 training, 1,000 validation, 1,000 test segments (pp. 9, 11).
test_conditions: Trained on UMa-NLoS, speed 10-100 km/h, SNR 0-30 dB; tested on it and on unseen UMi-NLoS and UMi-LoS without retraining, TDD and FDD (pp. 9, 11).
baselines: Non-learned: PAD [43], naive prediction. Learned: LSTM [24], STNN [44], Transformer [11], Linformer [45], Channelformer [12]; ablation variants (pp. 9, 13).
metrics: NMSE of predicted CSI, spectral efficiency (bps/Hz), transfer gap (%), parameters, FLOPs, inference time (pp. 9, 11, 12).
complexity: Table IV: 4.65 M parameters, 45.103 M FLOPs, 3.93 ms inference vs Transformer 7.50 M, 77.652 M, 9.24 ms; per-module O() analysis (pp. 8, 12).
q1_support: p. 8: "Channel datasets compliant with the 3rd generation partnership project (3GPP) standards [38], [39]"; p. 9: "quasi deterministic radio channel generator (QuaDRiGa) simulator [42], considering the urban macro non-line-of-sight (UMa-NLoS) and urban micro non-line-of-sight (UMi-NLoS) channel models"; reference [38] is 3GPP TR 38.901.
q2_support: p. 11: "trained on the UMa-NLOS scenario and tested on two previously unseen UMi-NLOS and UMi-LOS scenarios"; p. 9: "evaluated across all test conditions without retraining".
q3_support: p. 9: "PAD: [43] The prony angular-delay (PAD) method estimates and extrapolates channel parameters in the angle-delay domain" (non-learned) and "LSTM: [24] LSTM networks employ gated units to effectively capture temporal correlations within the channel sequence" (learned; also Transformer [11], Channelformer [12]); NMSE in Figs. 4-7 (p. 10), SE in Table II (p. 11).
q4_support: p. 12: "ChannelMamba achieves a competitive model size (in terms of parameters) while requiring significantly fewer FLOPs compared to attention-based models"; Table IV lists 4.65 M parameters, 45.103 M FLOPs, 3.93 ms inference time; p. 8 gives the O() analysis.
q5_support: p. 2, footnote 1: "Our source code is available at https://github.com/RxqJkb/ChannelMamba"
notes: Title and DOI on page 1 match. Area 2: channel (CSI) prediction, listed in area 2. System check passes: the BS has 32 ports (p. 9) although the UE has one omni-directional antenna. q1: QuaDRiGa generator, 3GPP-compliant scenarios with reference [38] = 3GPP TR 38.901 (p. 8, p. 14). q2: direct transfer to unseen UMi scenarios, transfer gap 10.6% and 16.0% for ChannelMamba (Table III, p. 11). Tables II to VI are images in the PDF, read from the page images; the Table IV values are from page 12. The authors state that validation on real measurements is future work (p. 14).
